newsitem.title: USA: U.S. may seek death penalty for Unabomber - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. may seek death penalty for Unabomber - report.

text.p: Federal prosecutors preparing for the upcoming murder trial of Unabomber suspect Theodore Kaczynski have requested that Attorney General Janet Reno seek the death penalty in his case, the Washington Post reported Thursday.

Quoting sources familiar with the deliberations, the newspaper said the request had been forwarded to a special Justice Department panel reviewing the case despite pleas from Kaczynski's relatives that his life be spared if he is convicted.
A final decision on the matter could be made public as early as Thursday, according to the report.

Prosecutors decided that while they were mindful of Kaczynski's family's wishes and other factors, the death penalty was warranted because they had uncovered volumes of evidence suggesting that the suspect was cold, calculating and exacting over 17 years of bombings that killed three people and injured 23 others, the Post said.
Investigators removed more than 6,000 pages of notes from Kaczynski's Montana cabin, much of it in diary-like form in which the suspect allegedly discusses his victims, the newspaper reported.
Grand juries in California and New Jersey have indicted Kaczynski on charges relating to the bombing deaths as well as several other attacks.
The 54-year-old, Harvard-educated mathematician is suspected of carrying out coast-to-coast bombing attacks and was the focus of the largest manhunt in U.S. history.
